stories.headline: A 2.2 kg fungus in China was so unique it got its own family
stories.summary: Dianjunus rex pushes pale yellow columns up through the forest floor, reaching about 50 cm with its buried black stalk. DNA showed it belongs to a brand-new fungal family.
stories.why: Even a fungus big enough to hold in 2 hands was unknown to science.

stories.stat_label: more sleep a day, in mice
stories.headline: Calming brain immune cells gave Alzheimer's mice 2+ hours of sleep
stories.summary: University of Kentucky scientists found overactive immune cells, not plaques, drove sleep loss. Removing most of them gave the mice over 2 extra hours of deep sleep a day.
stories.why: It points to a new way to help sleep in Alzheimer's, though it's not tested in people yet.

stories.headline: A dying star that came back to life is heating up again
stories.summary: Sakurai's Object reignited in the 1990s and hid behind dust. Using the Very Large Telescope, astronomers measured it again: about 30,500 K, its 1st temperature reading since 1998.
stories.why: Only 2 'born-again' stars have ever been caught changing in a human lifetime.

stories.headline: A ship wrecked in 1873 may have been found near Patagonia
stories.summary: On a remote island, archaeologists found a 19th-century ship's timbers and a castaway camp with bottles, buttons and tools. They likely belong to Luis Piedra Buena's stranded crew.
stories.why: The castaways built a boat from the wreck and sailed to safety in Chile.

fun_fact: Only 2 'born-again' stars have been seen reigniting: Sakurai's Object and V605 Aquilae.
